note: Claims the deferredRememberOpening rows parked by slice 3 in dividers-v1.json. Every row is replayed through the RENDERED shell in both projections; `remembered` is read back from the single dock-state seam, never from shell internals.

steps.why: opens into an empty dock, so the dock takes the panel's declared width
a fractional drag (reachable from clientX) is stored half-up in BOTH shells: 520.5 -> 521, never 520 by banker's rounding
the user gives the opening panel a width
anything opened after joins the stack at that width and does not change it
a forced arrangement clears with the dock; a remembered width describes one panel and survives
closing back to one panel does not re-narrow the dock
a different opening panel gets its own declared width, not pilot's remembered one
clamped up to the pane minimum
re-opened into an empty dock at the width it was last read at
below two panes' worth of space the panel is a sheet: no dock width, no dock separator

rememberedWidthCases.why: the gallery App Shell story's own mount shape: six declared panels, all open at once, dragged through the outer separator. The gate route drags it and reads the aside's real box, so the unit suites replay the same mount.

steps.why: a live drag grows the dock by the pointer delta whatever the rest of the stack is; the tolerance rules apply to RESTORED state, never to a gesture

rememberedWidthCases.why: the rendered shell, not just the model function: at a 1600px shell with the 216px rail on screen the ceiling is 1600-216-420=964, so a drag that asks for 1200 puts 964 on the aside and remembers 964. railCapable is declared so both lanes agree on the rail being in the row.

steps.why: past the floor: clamp(1200, 300, 964) = 964, and the dock right edge stays inside the row

rememberedWidthCases.why: W=900 with the 216px rail on screen: the expanded class is 840 wide, so a pane and the 420 content floor cannot fit beside the rail (216+300+420=936). Nothing docks. Before the capacity counted the rail the shell rendered a docked 300 and pushed 936px into a 900px row.

A non-class viewport: W=1250 with the rail on screen has a ceiling of 614, so a drag asking for 1200 must render 614 in BOTH lanes. A lane that clamps against the breakpoint CLASS width (1200) answers 564 - a 50px divergence at this width, and up to ~340px at others.

innerWidth 1300 (class large) but the shell box measures 900: the class the MEASURED width falls in is expanded (840), which cannot seat a pane and the 420 content floor beside the 216px rail (216+300+420=936). Nothing docks. When capacity was counted from the viewport class the shell rendered a docked 300 and pushed 936px into a 900px box.

roundTrip.why: open order, splitter sizes and remembered widths all survive serialise -> deserialise; the derived layout would be [0.5,0.5] in declared order, so an ignored snapshot cannot pass.

staleOrMalformed.why: a fractional persisted width (reachable from clientX) restores half-up in both projections: 640.5 -> 641, never 640 by banker's rounding

dockWidthProperty.why: The dock's width and the shell's pane CAPACITY are one model answer, not two. The ceiling on a dock width is W - R - F (measured shell inline size W, rail R, content floor F = 420) and the effective width is clamp(D, PaneMinimumWidth, ceiling) for every requested D alike - dragged, remembered or restored. Capacity counts the rail against the CLASS width of the measured shell - the narrowest row in that class - so placement stays constant inside a class (adaptation-v1 classPlacementCases) and a class that cannot seat one pane beside the rail docks nothing at all: the newest-opened panel is a sheet (slice 2), not an overflow. So rail + dock + floor <= W always holds. W is the MEASURED shell inline size in BOTH lanes, never the class width - those differ by up to 340px. Replayed against the model in both lanes; the stylesheet only paints flex:0 0 var(--hl-app-shell-dock-size).

dockPlacementProperty.why: OFF-DIAGONAL. The viewport class and the measured container are an independent PAIR, so the grid crosses viewport (media-query class) with measured container width. Pane capacity is counted from the class the MEASURED width falls in - the same width the clamp uses - so rail + dock + content floor <= the measured width, or nothing is docked at all. The viewport class drives sheet CHROME only (bottom sheet in compact, side sheet elsewhere). When capacity was counted from the viewport class instead, a 900px scene inside a 1300px viewport with the 216px rail docked a clamped 300 and pushed 936px into a 900px row. RE-MEASUREMENT: every row is also replayed as a RE-RENDER of the same mounted shell (Blazor via [JSInvokable] ShellMeasured and via the ShellInlineSize parameter, React by firing the ResizeObserver again) to remeasuredWidth - the invariant must hold after the second measurement too, so no cache may be keyed on anything less than every input the placement reads.

railToggleCase.why: The rail takes the row space before the dock does, so it is an input to PLACEMENT as much as the measured width: collapsing it inside one measured box (900, expanded class) frees 216px and the capacity goes 0 -> 1. Replayed as a re-render of the mounted shell.

dockTreeRetentionProperty.why: The AUTHORED tree - the arrangement the user dragged or the host restored - is a different thing from the DERIVED placement, so the two carry different invalidation sets and must not share one cache. Placement (container kinds, capacity) and the width clamp derive PER RENDER from every input; the authored tree is remembered against {open panels, spread, PLACEMENT class} only - the class the MEASURED width falls in. So a re-measurement inside one class keeps the arrangement, crossing a class falls back to the derived tree (slice 2's rule: placement is constant inside a class, so a tree authored in one class does not describe another), and coming BACK to the class the tree was authored in restores it together with the remembered widths. The rail is not in the key at all: it changes placement and the clamp, never what the user arranged. Persistence emits the tree only while it is the authored one - a derived reset is never written back, or the host would reload it as if the user had asked for it.

cases.why: 1300 -> 1400 is one re-measurement inside the large class: capacity 2 -> 2, kinds docked,docked throughout, nothing about placement moves. The authored 0.25/0.75 must survive it; the derived tree would be 0.5/0.5, which is the discriminator.

1300 -> 1700 crosses large into extra-large. Placement is constant inside a class, so a tree authored at large does not describe extra-large: the shell falls back to the derived even split and stops emitting the authored tree.

Leaving the class must not DESTROY the arrangement, only stop applying it: 1600 -> 900 derives (and re-clamps the remembered 640 to the 480 the 900 box allows), and 1600 again restores both the docked layout and the remembered width. A shell that overwrites the authored tree when it re-derives cannot come back.

The rail is an input to placement and to the clamp (the remembered 1000 is held at the 964 ceiling while the rail is on screen, and reaches 1000 when it collapses) but it is NOT part of what the user arranged, so it is not in the tree's key: the 0.25/0.75 survives the toggle while the capacity stays 3.

dockRestoreMeasurementProperty.why: Restore and FIRST measurement. Persisted state is applied only against a MEASURED placement class: until the box has been measured the restored tree is held PENDING - rendered, so the first paint is the arrangement the user left rather than a derived guess that flashes, but unstamped and NEVER emitted. Stamping it with the pre-measurement viewport class is the defect this property exists for: a narrow scene inside a wide viewport (viewport 1600, first measurement 1300) then reads as a class crossing, the shell derives 0.5/0.5, emits tree:null, and the host persists the loss for good. The grid is viewport x measured x rail with measured != viewport on 8 of its 12 rows, which is exactly what the slice 4 retention property could not see. After the first measurement the tree is stamped with the class it was measured in and behaves per slice 4: a genuine crossing derives HONESTLY (the derived tree is rendered and emitted as no tree, never as if authored) and coming back restores it. The mount (pre-measurement) point asserts container kinds, the authored fractions, that NOTHING has been emitted, and that the guessed dock still fits inside the viewport - but NOT an exact width: the fallback each shell guesses with before its first measurement is the one thing the two lanes genuinely cannot share. React reads window.innerWidth; Blazor has only media-query booleans and so falls back to the breakpoint CLASS floor, which at viewport 1300 with the rail on screen is 564 against React's 640. That divergence is PRE-EXISTING, it lives only in the unmeasured window, and it is why this slice suppresses the emit until the box is measured rather than trying to make two different guesses agree. Every post-measurement point below asserts the exact width in both shells.

dockSettlementProperty.why: Settlement, not the observer's first word. Measurement is settled only by a report the shell ACCEPTS (width > 0): a shell mounted hidden - a collapsed tab, a display:none route, a content-visibility subtree - reports 0 first, and treating that as measured stamps the restored tree with the pre-measurement VIEWPORT class, so the real width that follows reads as a class crossing and the host is handed tree:null - the loss slice 6 exists to prevent, reached through a different door than the 12-cell grid opens. The reset row is the other half of the same unmeasured window: Reset panels must clear the PENDING restored root, or the click is invisible until the box is measured. Blazor is immune to both by construction (measuredInlineSize takes only widths > 0; ResetDock clears pendingRestoredRoot) and these rows hold it to that; React needed both. A step with no expectedWidth key asserts no width: in the unmeasured window the guess is the one number the two lanes cannot share (see dockRestoreMeasurementProperty.why), which is exactly why nothing is emitted there.

cases.why: Mounted hidden inside a 1600 viewport: the first observer report is 0. That report settles nothing - the arrangement is still only SHOWN, unstamped and unemitted. The first REAL measurement (760, medium) stamps the authored 0.25/0.75 tree with the class it was measured in and emits it once, as the tree.
Mounted hidden and never measured: one zero-width report and nothing else. Nothing is stamped and NOTHING is written back to the host - a shell that never became visible must not persist a guess.

Reset panels clicked in the unmeasured window: the pending restored root is cleared, so the derived 0.5/0.5 layout is on screen immediately in BOTH shells rather than after the box is measured. The measurement that follows emits the reset state once, honestly as no tree.
